items.title: Concrete sentences supporting understanding
items.check: The document contains concrete, detailed sentences that demonstrate understanding of the topic, not vague statements like "I understand X".

items.title: Applicability conditions
items.check: The document describes who would use this, when, and where it applies.

items.title: License and copyright information
items.check: The document includes license and copyright information for any quoted or referenced source material, in the Meta Information section.

items.title: Clear input and output
items.check: For any algorithm or model described, the input and output are clearly and explicitly specified (types, shapes, or formats as applicable).

items.title: Algorithms described with pseudocode
items.check: Any algorithm is described with pseudocode or an equivalent step-by-step formalism, not only prose.

items.title: Datasets explicitly explained
items.check: Any dataset used or referenced is explicitly explained (what it contains, its size or scale, and why it is relevant).

items.title: Clear calculation order
items.check: The order in which computations happen is unambiguous (e.g. via numbered steps, a pipeline diagram, or explicit sequencing language).

items.title: Differentiation from similar algorithms
items.check: The document describes how this algorithm or technique differs from similar/competing algorithms or techniques.

items.title: Move provenance and sourcing honesty
items.check: For each named move, the document states its known origin/originator and era when sources establish one, and explicitly flags when sources disagree or are too thin to confirm a detail (rather than presenting an unverified claim as settled fact).

items.title: Concrete body mechanics
items.check: Each move is described in terms of concrete body mechanics (which joints or body parts move, and on which beat/count), not vague language like "feel the groove".

items.title: Style/family attribution
items.check: Each move states which dance style or family it belongs to (e.g. Hip-Hop, Locking, Popping, Breaking), so it is not mislabeled across styles.

items.title: Requested move coverage
items.check: When specific named moves were requested for a style's basic-steps document, each requested move is covered explicitly by its own name (not only implied by a generic groove description).

items.title: No piece-movement rules
items.check: The document does not explain how individual pieces move (that is assumed prior knowledge); it focuses on strategic principles and named concepts instead.

items.title: Reasoning behind principles
items.check: For each principle, opening family, or endgame technique named, the document explains why it works (the underlying strategic or tactical reasoning), not only its name.

items.title: Concept categorization
items.check: Each named opening family or endgame technique states which broader category it belongs to (e.g. open game vs. closed game; king-side vs. queen-side endgame), so unrelated concepts are not conflated.

items.title: Game-phase scope discipline
items.check: A document under chess/opening/ stays within opening-phase concepts, and a document under chess/ending/ stays within endgame-phase concepts; middlegame-specific content does not creep into either.
